alignments.note: Inflected imperative takes its supplied subject pronoun as a rule 7/9 helper; head on the lexical verb.
Case preposition *of* rides with the pronoun under rule 21; head on the noun-equivalent word.
Rule 82: the answering καί is inside the crasis and has its own English word (*also*), so the comparative keeps *even as* whole, headed on *as*.

Crasis under rule 55 takes both the conjunction word (*also*) and the pronoun (*I*); the predicate is a genitive noun phrase, so under rules 53 and 63 the supplied copula *am* stays with the subject pronoun.
Genitive noun rendered *of + noun*; head on the noun under rule 17.

review_notes: The correlative *even as* is given whole to καθώς because the crasis already carries its own *also*; giving *even* to the crasis under rule 82's bare-*even* clause remains defensible but that clause is scoped to where no correlative word is written for the καί.
